very upset. The instructions said to use a 3/16" drill bit which I had to pay $10 for. Once hol...

very upset. The instructions said to use a 3/16" drill bit which I had to pay $10 for. Once holes were drilled, the included screws were too small for the drilled holes. Now, I have holes in my ceramic tile AND the cement backing. I will have to go back out again, buy bigger screws that fit in the grab bar holes, come home again to install the thing once and for all. This should have been an easy install but it has taken a lot of my time to retrofit the solution. Bad move on the part of Kohler. I called Kohler to report the issue. I waited on hold for 15 minutes to speak to a human being. Customer Service rep. Monique was rude beyond belief, put me on hold again and then transferred my to the Technical Dept. which was the number I pressed in the call tree in the first place. 30 minutes later, Kohlet tells me that I should have only drilled through the ceramic tile. Problem is I had to also drill through the concrete backing. I will now use wall anchors, different screws and different drill bits because Kohler should know that not everyone puts tile against drywall or wood. Huge pain, poor instructions!

by SusanC

Sep 28, 2021

This is an Assist Bar, not a Grab Bar

A grab bar must be ADA compliant and at least 1-1/4-inch in diameter and have 1-1/2-inch clearance to the mounting surface. At 7/8-inch diameter, this product is an assist bar and provides a comfortable grip but is only 1-5/16-inches from the mounting surface. Construction is all stainless-steel including the #10 X 2-inch mounting screws—three for each end. Mounting the bar is a problematic unless there is continuous blocking between the studs at the desired location. The mounting plate holes on either side of the bar are spaced 1-1/8-inch apart which would only allow for 3/16-inch edge distance on a 1-1/2-inch stud, which is not practical. For a vertical installation, there are staggered holes that are spaced on 3/8-inch centers which would allow for mounting on a stud, but only on one side of the mounting plate. The screws should be placed on the side opposite the direction that force will be applied. For horizontal installation, one side can be securely mounted on a stud, but you will need special mounting hardware, such as WINGITS, for the other end. The instructions do not address installation on studs well very well. My application was to mount the bar on a horizontal wooden surface on top of a knee wall with a 2 X 4 underneath, so I did not have a problem. See photo. NEXT. The brushed finish is very uniform, and escutcheons are provided to cover the screws in the mounting plates. There are four indentations in the escutcheon

## FAQ

#### Can I install this on my fiberglass tub surround?

Yes, the metal grab bar is suitable for fiberglass or acrylic surrounds as well as plaster or drywall. With additional hardware the grab bar can also be mounted on ceramic tile surrounds.

#### How much weight will it hold? Is it a true grab bar or only a stabilizer?

It is a sturdy metal grab bar providing additional stability and securely supporting up to 440 pounds.

#### Can the grab bar be installed with screws or with suction cups?

The metal grab bar can only be installed with screws and wall anchors where appropriate.

#### Does the metal grab bar include screws for installing it?

Yes! The metal grab bar includes six 2” screws and six wall anchors suitable for installing on most surfaces.

#### Should the grab bar be placed horizontally or vertically?

The metal grab bar can be placed in any position, horizontally, vertically or diagonally for optimal support in the desired location.

#### Is this grab bar only for the bathroom?

No, the grab bar can be installed on wall surface for additional support where needed.

#### Is the stainless steel shiny?

The metal grab bar features a brushed nickel finish.

#### Does the grab bar include flanges to hide the mounting hardware?

Yes! Each grab bar includes decorative flanges that securely lock in place after installation for a clean, sleek appearance.

#### Is the metal bar rust proof for use in the shower?

Yes! The stainless steel grab bar is resistant to rust and corrosion for use in the bathtub or shower.

#### Will the metal grab bar work in a tiled bathroom?

Yes! The metal grab bar can safely be installed on tile with additional mounting hardware.

#### Can I use this to pull myself up from sitting in the tub?

Yes, the metal grab bar can be installed diagonally in most bathtubs for additional assistance in exiting the tub.

#### Does the bar have to be installed into a stud?

Ideally, the grab bar should be installed into a stud, however, the set includes wall anchors for securing the grab bar to the wall if necessary.
